expected.reason: id 999 is a higher build number and STABLE-channel, so it would normally win the highest-id comparison -- but its `downloads` object has no `server:default.url` field, so the guard at line 244-247 (`guard let downloads = ..., serverDefault = ..., urlString = ..., downloadURL = URL(string: urlString) else { continue }`) skips it entirely via `continue` before it's ever compared against `bestId`. The scan continues to the next entry (real id 132, which has a valid download) and selects that instead.

notes: A missing/malformed download URL on an otherwise-qualifying build entry does not abort the whole fetch and does not even get compared as a worse candidate -- it is invisible to the `bestId`/`bestOption` tracking entirely (the `continue` at line 247 fires before either variable is touched). This means a single corrupted entry higher up in the real build list can never accidentally suppress a good lower entry from being found; the same guard shape (`downloads["server:default"]` -> `url` -> parseable `URL`) appears identically in `ServerJarProviders.PaperDownloader.downloadVersion` (ServerJarProviders.swift:230-239) for the simpler create-flow download path, not just this Components-tab helper.
